sources.title: Epistemology in the Age of Large Language Models
sources.local_copy: docs/papers/Epistemology in the Age of Large Language Models Mugleston(2025).pdf
inspected_anchors: Sections 3.1-3.3 pp6-8: belief, justification and Gettier discussion
Section 5 pp9-10: understanding and informative versus repetitive coherence
Sections 6-8 pp10-15: Chinese room, context, epistemic tools and reliance
Section 9 pp15-17: provisional knowledge claims and stated thought-experiment purpose; references pp17-19
supported_claims: The authors discuss whether internal representations qualify as knowledge, distinguishing this philosophical question from established justified true belief.
The article identifies limitations of repeated consistency and ends with unresolved claims about understanding.
This is philosophical context, not a banking identification theorem or replicated package benchmark.
forbidden_claims: Do not import its secondary empirical scores as independently checked primary evidence
Do not import its broad statements about current LLM access/training/journal policies as current facts
Do not treat philosophical discussion as banking evidence or an identification result
